name: Air Receiver Tanks
title: Air Receiver Tank Manufacturer, Coimbatore | WRV 250–10,000 L
description: WRV compressed air receiver tanks, 250–10,000 litres standard, 7 to 12.5 bar g working pressure, hydrostatically tested, ASME VIII on request. Win Equipments.
card: Hydro-tested pressure vessels that store air and settle condensate.
lede: An air receiver stores compressed air, steadies pressure for the plant and gives condensate somewhere to settle before it travels down the line. Every WRV vessel is designed to requirement and hydrostatically tested, with ASME VIII fabrication available on request.
highlights: Fabricated to ASME VIII on requirement

principle.intro: Air drawn into a compressor carries moisture. Compression raises its temperature and its capacity to hold water vapour; when the air cools again, that vapour condenses.

stages.name: Store
stages.text: The receiver stores compressed air and evens out pressure swings between compressor and plant demand.

stages.name: Cool
stages.text: Air slows and cools in the vessel, so part of the condensate drops out downstream of the compressor.

stages.name: Drain
stages.text: Condensate collects at the bottom and is removed through the drain; the air leaving is still saturated and needs drying.

applications: Compressed air plants of all sizes
Dry receiver after the dryer and filters

faqs.a: Each standard WRV size is offered at 7, 10 or 12.5 bar g working pressure, with design pressures of 8, 11 and 14 bar g and hydrostatic test pressures of 12, 17 and 21 bar g.
Yes. Vessels can be fabricated to ASME VIII on requirement.

faqs.q: Do I need a wet and a dry receiver?
faqs.a: A typical installation uses a wet receiver after the compressor to settle condensate, and a dry receiver after the dryer and filters to buffer clean, dry air for the plant.
